title: Before Elisha's Gate
description: Before Elisha's Gate in Tonic Solfa to DARWALL, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 38, “Naaman. 2Ki 5:14”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DARWALL; any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-fore El-i-sha's gate The Syr-ian le-per stood; But could not brook to wait, He deemed him-self too good: He thought the pro-phet would at-tend, And not to him a mes-sage send.

lines: But could not brook to wait,
He thought the prophet would attend,
And not to him a message send.
And will he not be seen?
I were as well at home,
Why must I wash in Jordan's flood?
Soon as his pride was brought to yield,
From sin to set me free,
When first I heard his fame:
Surely, thought I, my pompous train
Of vows and tears will notice gain.
Had he some painful task enjoined,
When by his word he spake,
Go wash, and thou art free:"
O! how did my proud heart gainsay,
I feared to trust this simple way.
I washed, and I was cured:
Which cleansed a wretch so vile as I.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to DARWALL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
